name: float-operations-decided-by-a-bound-constant-fast
rationale: The float operations of a module compiled with fast math whose operand is a function constant, so what each folds to is known only once the constants are bound. Constant 0 is +0 and 1 is -0 (float), 2 a quiet NaN with its sign set and a payload (0xffc12345), 3 a signalling NaN (0x7f800321), 4 and 5 the half zeros and 6 a signalling half NaN with its sign set (0xfd21). Each thread reads one float4 x and writes one Rows record: f[0..3) x times a zero of each sign in each operand order, f[3..5) a fused multiply-add with a NaN addend and a NaN first factor beside x, f[5..11) operations of constants alone with NaNs in each order (an addition, a product, a NaN times a zero, a subtraction, a quotient and a fused multiply-add), and h[0..3) the half zero products and fused multiply-add over half4(x). The lanes x are the infinities, a NaN, -2.5, 2.5, both zeros and 0.5, so a product the device computes from an infinity or a NaN differs from one decided by its zero operand, and an operation the device computes from a NaN operand may answer other bits than the constant's. The 8 bytes past each record are outside every write and pin the 0xCD fill. The additions, subtractions, products and quotients of a NaN constant and x under fast math, whose nnan makes them poison and whose store Metal drops, are sfold_fast_poison's and not compared here.

name: nan-model-min-max-at-zeros-and-denormals-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_minmax_fast (nan_minmax's program under the default fast math, the flagged state) at zeros and denormals: Lane i reads (a, b, c) and writes fmin(a, b), fmax(a, b), a < b ? a : b, a > b ? a : b, min3, max3, median3, and clamp(a, b, c). Lanes: every pair of +0, -0, +-2^-149, the largest denormal, +-2^-126, and 1, each with two third operands from the same set: which operand a tie of zeros answers, and whether a comparison reads a denormal as zero. Every operand is loaded from a buffer; the output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: nan-model-min-max-of-nan-operands-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_minmax_fast (nan_minmax's program under the default fast math: fmin, fmax, min3, max3, median3, and clamp are the fast_ calls; the flagged state) at nan_minmax's lanes. Which NaN or number Metal's min and max answer: lane i reads (a, b, c) and writes fmin(a, b), fmax(a, b) (min and max are the same calls), a < b ? a : b, a > b ? a : b (fcmp and select), min3, max3, median3, and clamp(a, b, c), over nan_arith's lanes. Compiled without fast math unless named; every operand is loaded from a buffer, so nothing folds but what the AIR shows. NaN operands: quiet and signaling of either sign with payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: reduce-two-channel-groups-with-the-scale-buffer-gated-off
rationale: MPSCNNGroupNormalization's gradient reduction, with the `scaleAndBiasDefined` function constant OFF so the `gamma` device buffer at Metal index 26 is not part of the function signature. That is the shape `passes/access/private_memory.rs::private_zero_pointer_for_type` keys on: the absent buffer becomes an unnamed null-initialized `Private` variable, and every access chain rooted in it is neutralized into a pointer at a fresh Private placeholder, so the load reads zero. 310 corpus modules reach that rule and no authored case did, and it is only reachable with the gating constant false -- with it true the buffer is present and no chain is neutralized. This is one of the smallest hosts at 227 lines. Metal agrees exactly: the gated-off buffer reads zero there too. Two threads in one threadgroup, four channels, two groups, two channels per group. Each thread dots one group's two channels of `_dLdGamma` against `gamma`, so the answer is +0 for both groups no matter what `_dLdGamma` holds -- 1, 2, 3 and 4 are chosen so any non-zero read from the absent buffer would show. Thread zero then takes the switch tail (`(num_groups + 3 & ~3) - num_groups` is 2) and writes +0 to the two padding groups. The selected region is twice the written footprint: the first sixteen bytes must be zero and the last sixteen must still be the authored 0xAB, so the case pins where the kernel writes as well as what it writes. Nothing here is computed in floating point beyond a multiply-add of zero, so the answer does not depend on rounding or fast-math association. Every params byte outside `channels`, `num_groups` and `channels_per_group` is 0xCC. `authored_bounded`: the group loop steps by `threads_per_threadgroup` (2) from the thread index and exits once the index reaches `num_groups` (2), so it runs exactly once per thread; the channel loop runs `channels_per_group` (2) times. Both bounds are authored literals no input can change.
